overview: The Council approved a multi-million dollar bond for a new police station and authorized a Statement of Interest to the state for renovations at Medford High School. They also held an extensive discussion on zoning reform to address neighborhood density and updated sewer connection fees for new construction.

items.title: Police Station Bond Package
items.summary: Approved the third reading of the bond package for the new police station after a motion to table for further cost analysis failed.

items.title: School Building Authority Statement of Interest
items.summary: Authorized the submission of a Statement of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority for potential funding for renovations, systems upgrades, and additions at Medford High School.

items.title: Law Department Claim Settlement
items.summary: Approved a settlement payment of $5,616 for a slip-and-fall claim against the city.

items.title: National Grid Grant of Location
items.summary: Approved the relocation of a gas main on Winthrop Street with a requirement to restrict construction during school rush hour periods.

items.title: Crosswalk and Roadway Striping Schedule
items.summary: Requested a restriping schedule from the DPW and discussed utilizing thermoplastic paint for more durable school crosswalks.

items.title: Corridor Zoning and Salem Street Density
items.summary: Requested a legal opinion on changing zoning incrementally by street and discussed resident petitions to downzone Salem Street to prevent high-density apartment development.

items.title: New Construction Sewer Connection Fees
items.summary: Voted to recommend updating sewer connection fees to be charged per fixture rather than per lateral for new construction projects.

items.title: Routine DPW and Property Updates
items.summary: Requested updates on Community Preservation Act commission appointments, the spring street sweeping schedule, and the status of the former Hegner Center property.

items.title: Wage Theft Ordinance and Replica Firearms
items.summary: Passed the first reading of an ordinance to prevent wage theft and referred a proposal to regulate replica firearms back to committee for further legal review.

items.title: City Hall Banners Petition
items.summary: Placed on file a resident petition arguing that displaying event banners on the exterior of City Hall is inappropriate and distracting.

items.title: Memorial Resolutions and Moments of Silence
items.summary: Extended condolences and held moments of silence for several deceased residents and city employees.
